explanation: The I50L mutation reduces atazanavir binding through loss of optimal van der Waals packing in the flap region. Isoleucine's branched β-carbon and larger hydrophobic surface area create favorable contacts with the inhibitor at the 2.2 Å minimum distance, whereas leucine's linear side chain cannot maintain equivalent shape complementarity with atazanavir's binding pocket geometry. This modest (~0.1 kcal/mol) destabilization reflects a localized packing defect rather than a dramatic conformational change, consistent with position 50's location at the periphery of the binding interface in the flap.
